output.argument_summary: 1. The draft-runbook point is narrower than the packet is being read: I am not claiming ISTRESS-DRAFT-MITIGATION-003-NEAR-MISS cures the current issue or satisfies the policy standard for caveat-free certification. I am using it only for the separate proposition that post-certification monitoring and rollback can be defined as risk-management handling once the limitation is disclosed. 2. On the launch-readiness question, ISTRESS-DRAFT-MITIGATION-003-AGGREGATE-PASS still matters. It supports that the release as a whole passed aggregate readiness and had no severity-one rehearsal incidents. That does not erase ISTRESS-DRAFT-MITIGATION-003-CURRENT-GAP, but it does distinguish overall deployment readiness from the narrower question of how certification must be worded. 3. The model-card concern is partly valid. ISTRESS-DRAFT-MITIGATION-003-CONTEXT shows the current draft says there are no known material limitations while also flagging reviewer concern about the Spanish billing issue. I am not asserting that disclosure already happened. I am asserting the certification defense is supportable only if certification is understood with that disclosure condition, consistent with ISTRESS-DRAFT-MITIGATION-003-POLICY and the public documentation principles in ISTRESS-DRAFT-MITIGATION-003-HF-CONTENT. 4. Materiality is the remaining evidentiary gap, but it cuts both ways. The record shows a named launch-use-case weakness in Spanish billing-ticket triage, so the auditor is justified not to treat this as clean certification. At the same time, the same record does not compel the stronger conclusion that the whole certification request should escalate beyond a caveated posture, because ISTRESS-DRAFT-MITIGATION-003-AGGREGATE-PASS and ISTRESS-DRAFT-MITIGATION-003-NIST-MEASURE support a measured, monitored, disclosed deployment framework rather than an all-or-nothing one. 5. So the packet should be read as defending certification in a bounded form: launch readiness passed; certification wording cannot honestly be caveat-free on this record; monitoring is relevant for management after disclosure, not proof of prior resolution; and the unsupported part should be narrowed rather than escalated as if the entire certification basis fails.

Separately, ISTRESS-DRAFT-MITIGATION-003-POLICY says material limitations for named launch use cases must be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. ISTRESS-DRAFT-MITIGATION-003-HF-CONTENT and ISTRESS-DRAFT-MITIGATION-003-NIST-MEASURE reinforce that distinction between disclosure/documentation and ongoing monitoring; they do not convert the draft artifact into approved mitigation.
